---
title: Features
description: Cache extension capabilities and backend details
---

## Cache Interface

Every backend implements the same `Cache` interface, and every value is a `[]byte`:

```go
type Cache interface {
    Connect(ctx context.Context) error
    Disconnect(ctx context.Context) error
    Ping(ctx context.Context) error
    Get(ctx context.Context, key string) ([]byte, error)
    Set(ctx context.Context, key string, value []byte, ttl time.Duration) error
    Delete(ctx context.Context, key string) error
    Exists(ctx context.Context, key string) (bool, error)
    Clear(ctx context.Context) error
    Keys(ctx context.Context, pattern string) ([]string, error)
    TTL(ctx context.Context, key string) (time.Duration, error)
    Expire(ctx context.Context, key string, ttl time.Duration) error
}
```

You don't call `Connect` and `Disconnect` yourself. The extension does that when the app starts and
stops, and every other method returns `ErrNotConnected` outside that window.

## Drivers

You pick the backend with the `Driver` field:

| Driver | Status |
|---|---|
| `inmemory` | Works. A map guarded by a `sync.RWMutex`, with a background sweep of expired entries |
| `redis` | Not implemented yet. Validation requires a `URL`, then service construction fails with "redis driver not yet implemented" |
| `memcached` | Not implemented yet. Same as `redis`, failing with "memcached driver not yet implemented" |

So for now the cache lives in one process. Two replicas of your service each have their own copy,
and a restart empties it.

## TTL-Based Expiration

Every entry can have its own TTL. A `Set` with `ttl == 0` uses `DefaultTTL` (5 minutes unless you
change it). `TTL` returns the time left, or `0` for an entry that never expires. `Expire` with a TTL
of `0` or less makes the entry permanent.

```go
// Set with an explicit TTL
err := c.Set(ctx, "token:abc", tokenBytes, time.Hour)

// Set with the default TTL from config
err = c.Set(ctx, "token:def", tokenBytes, 0)

// Inspect the remaining TTL
remaining, err := c.TTL(ctx, "token:abc")

// Change the TTL on an existing key
err = c.Expire(ctx, "token:abc", 2*time.Hour)
```

`Get`, `TTL` and `Expire` return `ErrNotFound` for a key that is missing or has expired.

## Automatic Cleanup

The in-memory backend runs a goroutine that removes expired entries every `CleanupInterval`
(1 minute by default), so entries nobody reads again don't pile up. It starts on `Connect` and stops
on `Disconnect`.

## Eviction

When the cache already holds `MaxSize` entries (10,000 by default), the next `Set` removes one entry
first:

1. It removes the first expired entry it finds.
2. If none has expired, it removes an arbitrary entry, whichever comes first in Go map order.

That is not LRU, so a hot key can go. If you need hot keys to survive, size `MaxSize` so you rarely
reach it, or set it to `0` for no limit. Each eviction increments the `cache_evict` counter.

## Key Prefixing

`Prefix` is added to every key on write and stripped again from `Keys` results, so several apps or
tenants can share a key space:

```go
// With Prefix "myapp:" configured, this stores "myapp:user:123"
err := c.Set(ctx, "user:123", data, 0)

// Keys returns "user:123", without the prefix
keys, err := c.Keys(ctx, "user:*")
```

## Size Guards

Every `Set` checks `MaxKeySize` (250 bytes by default) and `MaxValueSize` (1 MiB by default). Over
either limit, it returns `ErrKeyTooLarge` or `ErrValueTooLarge` and stores nothing. A value of `0`
turns the check off. An empty key returns a plain error.

## Glob-Style Key Listing

`Keys(ctx, pattern)` supports one `*` per pattern:

- `"*"` matches every key
- `"user:*"` is a prefix match
- `"*:sessions"` is a suffix match
- `"app:*:config"` matches prefix and suffix

A pattern with two wildcards, such as `"*:draft:*"`, matches nothing. `Keys` also walks every entry
while holding the read lock, so keep it off hot request paths when your cache is large.

## Metrics

The in-memory backend increments these counters through `forge.Metrics`:

| Counter | Incremented when |
|---|---|
| `cache_hit` | `Get` finds a live entry |
| `cache_miss` | `Get` finds no entry, or an expired one |
| `cache_set` | `Set` stores a value |
| `cache_delete` | `Delete` runs |
| `cache_clear` | `Clear` runs |
| `cache_evict` | An entry is removed because the cache reached `MaxSize` |

## Health Checks

`CacheService.Health` calls the backend's `Ping`, which returns `ErrNotConnected` until the cache has
started. The extension's own `Health` only reports whether the extension has started.

## Extra Interfaces (In-Memory)

The in-memory backend implements two typed interfaces on top of `Cache`. The `cache.Cache` you get
from the container is the `*CacheService` wrapper, which doesn't have these methods, so ask the
service for its backend and type-assert it:

```go
svc, err := forge.Inject[*cache.CacheService](app.Container())
if err != nil {
	return err
}

sc, ok := svc.Cache().(cache.StringCache)
if !ok {
	return errors.New("backend does not support string helpers")
}

if err := sc.SetString(ctx, "greeting", "hello", 5*time.Minute); err != nil {
	return err
}

greeting, err := sc.GetString(ctx, "greeting") // "hello"
```

### JSONCache

`SetJSON` marshals any Go value and `GetJSON` unmarshals it into a target:

```go
type User struct {
	Name  string `json:"name"`
	Email string `json:"email"`
}

jc, ok := svc.Cache().(cache.JSONCache)
if !ok {
	return errors.New("backend does not support JSON helpers")
}

if err := jc.SetJSON(ctx, "user:1", User{Name: "Alice", Email: "alice@example.com"}, 0); err != nil {
	return err
}

var user User
err = jc.GetJSON(ctx, "user:1", &user) // user.Name == "Alice"
```

### CounterCache and MultiCache

| Interface | Methods |
|---|---|
| `CounterCache` | `Incr`, `IncrBy`, `Decr`, `DecrBy` |
| `MultiCache` | `MGet`, `MSet`, `MDelete` |

Both are declared in the package, but no backend implements them yet, so a type assertion to either
one fails.

## Sentinel Errors

| Error | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ErrNotFound` | `Get`, `TTL` or `Expire` on a key that is missing or expired |
| `ErrNotConnected` | Any call before the app has started the cache, or after it stopped |
| `ErrKeyTooLarge` | Key longer than `MaxKeySize` bytes |
| `ErrValueTooLarge` | Value larger than `MaxValueSize` bytes |
| `ErrInvalidTTL` | A negative `DefaultTTL` in the config |
| `ErrUnsupportedOperation` | Declared for backends that lack an operation. The in-memory backend never returns it |

Compare them with `errors.Is`.
